content: Within this narrative of progress Ibn Turka hails Akhlāṭī as a pioneer precisely in his status as restorer of occult philosophy in the late eighth/fourteenth century after a long lapse; Melvin-Koushki's footnote quotes the R. Ḥurūf as saying knowledge of this science had been all but erased long since and is being revived in our day through the efforts of Akhlāṭī's disciples.
